newsitem.title: USA: FBI interviews airline crew about flare-like object.
newsitem.headline: FBI interviews airline crew about flare-like object.

text.p: The FBI is interviewing a Saudi Arabian Airlines crew about a flare-like object they saw in the sky in New York while approaching Kennedy International Airport, federal law enforcement officials said on Thursday.
The spokesman said the crew reported that the light was in the vicinity of the flight path of TWA Flight 800, which crashed off Long Island in July. He gave no further details.
The FBI questioned the crew at Washington's Dulles International Airport, the plane's next stop.
The FBI was interested because investigators have still not determined the cause of the Flight 800 crash, with theories ranging from a bomb, missile or mechanical failure.
The officials were at a loss to explain what the Saudi crew had observed. "It could be anything," one official said.
They also were unsure what significance, if any, it would have for the TWA investigation, which has enountered problems in pinpointing the cause of the crash.
"It may turn out to be completely nothing. I can't say there is anything to it. Obviously, if someone reports something, they have to check it out. That's standard," one official said.
A Federal Aviation Administration official said the crew of the 747, flying at about 12,000 feet (4,000 metres), spotted the green flare while making the approach to Kennedy.
But, the official said, the pilot did not feel the plane was in jeopardy and simply reported it as a "sighting."
A month ago a Pakistan Airlines crew also reported seeing a light in the sky after leaving New York.
